MSDE partners with Ministry of Jal Shakti to skill one lakh youth under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
articles.full_content:
The initiative will leverage the nationwide network of ITIs and NSTIs to develop a skilled workforce for rural water supply operations and maintenance
In an effort to align vocational training with emerging employment opportunities in the rural water sector, the Directorate General of Training (DGT), under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti. The partnership will focus on implementing the Water Supply Operation & Maintenance Skilling Programme (Nal Jal Mitra) under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.
The initiative aims to train and certify at least one lakh candidates, with an estimated financial outlay of ₹111.93 crore, entirely funded by DDWS.
The MoU was signed in the presence of Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; Shri C. R. Patil, Union Minister of Jal Shakti; and Shri V. Somanna, Minister of State, Jal Shakti.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, underscored that the initiative represents a significant example of inter-ministerial convergence aimed at addressing the skilled manpower requirements of a key national programme. He highlighted that the country's extensive network of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) offers an effective platform for imparting specialised skills required for rural water supply operations and maintenance.
The 165-hour training programme has been developed by the Central Staff Training and Research Institute (CSTARI) under DGT, in consultation with DDWS. It will be offered as an optional elective to existing and former trainees of the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) Fitter and Plumber trades across ITIs and NSTIs.
The programme combines 120 hours of institutional training with 45 hours of mandatory on-the-job training. Candidates will learn plumbing, water distribution, pump and motor maintenance, basic electrical work and water quality monitoring. Upon successful completion, trainees will receive a National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF)-aligned short-term training certificate from DGT in addition to their National Trade Certificate (NTC).
The National Instructional Media Institute (NIMI), under DGT, will oversee training coordination, assessment, certification and fund disbursement. DDWS will make the details of certified candidates available at the district and Gram Panchayat levels, where they may be engaged for work as per the policies of the respective states.
Nearly 16 crore rural households in India now have tap water connections. Keeping these water supply systems functional requires trained personnel at the village level. The programme seeks to meet this requirement and, in the process, open up employment avenues for rural youth.

Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and Data Security Council of India (DSCI) sign MoU to enable trusted data sharing for official statistics
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and the Data Security Council of India (DSCI), set up by Nasscom, a not-for-profit industry body and think tank on data protection and cyber security, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in New Delhi today. Dr Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI, Shri Vinayak Godse, Chief Executive Officer, DSCI, and senior officers of the Ministry were present on the occasion. The MoU forms part of the Ministry’s efforts to strengthen the National Statistical System through collaboration with public and private sector institutions.
Statistical agencies now-a-days use data from both traditional and alternative sources, some of which contain personal identifiers. With Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 scheduled to come into force in 2027, data producing agencies need to gear up themselves by reviewing how they handle such data while maintaining privacy and confidentiality. This partnership will help develop protocols for sharing data in trusted manner within and across agencies while maintaining data quality, protecting privacy and preserving statistical confidentiality. As a first step, MoSPI and DSCI will jointly prepare a policy paper on trusted data flows and data management, drawing on international good practices in data protection and cybersecurity.
The collaboration will also cover joint research on data governance and technical support for the adoption of privacy-enhancing technologies and the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI). The MoU also provides facilitation for pilot projects with industry, academia, research institutions and international organisations and it will strengthen the national statistical ecosystem, by enabling responsible adoption of AI and emerging technologies.

Dr Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI, Shri Vinayak Godse, Chief Executive Officer, DSCI, and senior officers of the Ministry were present on the occasion. The MoU forms part of the Ministry’s efforts to strengthen the National Statistical System through collaboration with public and private sector institutions.

PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry Records ₹4,385.28 Crore Incentive Disbursement in FY 2026–27
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) continues to strengthen India's automobile and auto component manufacturing ecosystem through the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry. The scheme aims to enhance domestic manufacturing capabilities, promote advanced automotive technologies and position India as a global hub for automobile manufacturing.
Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel, Shri H. D. Kumaraswamy, chaired a review meeting with Dr. Hanif Qureshi, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI), today to review the progress and implementation of the PLI-Auto Scheme.
Accelerated Incentive Disbursement under the PLI-Auto Scheme
With a total approved budgetary outlay of ₹25,938 crore, the PLI-Auto Scheme has made significant progress in promoting investments, strengthening domestic supply chains and encouraging the manufacturing of Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products. During FY 2026–27, incentive disbursements under the scheme reached ₹4,385.28 crore as of 25 th November 2026. The cumulative incentive disbursement under the scheme since its inception has reached ₹6,771.64 crore.
Strong Investment, Incremental Sales and Employment Generation
The scheme has also recorded encouraging progress in attracting investments and generating employment. As of 30 th September 2026, approved applicants had reported cumulative investments of ₹52,806 crore, surpassing the targeted investment of ₹42,500 crore. The scheme has also facilitated incremental sales of ₹82,993 crore over the base year FY 2019–20 and generated 77,755 employment opportunities, reflecting its contribution to strengthening India's automotive manufacturing ecosystem.
Strengthening Domestic Manufacturing and Value Addition
Promoting domestic value addition remains a key objective of the PLI-Auto Scheme. The scheme mandates a minimum Domestic Value Addition (DVA) of 50% for eligible products to qualify for incentives. As of 25 th November 2026, DVA certificates have been issued to 9 Champion OEMs covering 139 products/variants, and 10 Component Champions covering 53 products/variants. This progress reflects the growing domestic capabilities in manufacturing advanced automotive products and components.
The initiative is aligned with the Government of India's vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat, reinforcing the country's commitment to becoming a leading global destination for automobile and auto component manufacturing. The Ministry of Heavy Industries remains committed to supporting the growth of a robust, resilient and technologically advanced automotive industry through sustained policy initiatives and industry collaboration.

Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas to visit PDEU; to see National Core Repository and interact with students on Energy Transition
articles.full_content:
Senior officers of ONGC and IOCL to accompany the Hon'ble Minister
HHon'ble Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Government of India, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, will visit Pandit Deendayal Energy University (PDEU), Gandhinagar, on Friday (27th November).. The Hon'ble Minister is scheduled to arrive on campus at 2:30 p.m. and will be accompanied by senior officers of Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) and Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL). During the visit, the Hon'ble Minister will tour the National Core Repository and will thereafter interact with a select group of PDEU students on the theme of Energy Transition.
National Core Repository
The National Core Repository (NCR) at Gandhinagar was established under the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH), Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, as a national facility for the preservation, curation and scientific study of drill cores recovered from India's sedimentary basins. Cores held at national repositories are treated as a national asset, with access governed by DGH, and constitute a primary scientific record of the country's subsurface. The facility supports basin studies, reservoir characterisation and exploration research by academia, national oil companies and industry.
PDEU will be housing about 1 lakh metre cores from onshore and offshore basins of India. To start with the university is focusing on 5 basins.
Interaction with students on Energy Transition
The Hon'ble Minister will address and take questions from students drawn from across the University's schools of petroleum technology, energy technology, management and liberal studies. The session is intended as an open exchange on India's energy transition pathway, the role of natural gas as a transition fuel, green hydrogen, biofuels and ethanol blending, carbon capture, and the skills and research capacity the sector will require of the next generation of energy professionals.
PDEU and the energy transition
The University was reconstituted from Pandit Deendayal Petroleum University to Pandit Deendayal Energy University in 2020, reflecting a deliberate widening of its mandate from hydrocarbons to the full energy spectrum. Research at the University today spans solar, wind, hydrogen, geothermal, bioenergy and energy storage, aligned to India's net-zero commitment.
Among the University's dedicated facilities are the Centre of Excellence for Geothermal Energy (CEGE), established in 2013 with the support of the Government of Gujarat; the Solar Research and Development Centre; the Centre for Biofuel and Bioenergy Studies; the International Automobile Centre of Excellence; and the SIEMENS Centre of Excellence. The Department of Science and Technology sanctioned a Technology Enabling Centre at PDEU in 2023 on the theme of Energy, Health and Water, to carry laboratory research through prototype, validation and field trial to industry adoption.

DPIIT Concludes Special Campaign 6 with Significant Achievements in Swachhata and Reduction of Pendency
articles.full_content:
Biomass Gasifier Installed at NCCBM’s Ballabgarh Campus to Promote Sustainable Waste-to-Energy Conversion DPIIT Achieves 100% Disposal of Public Grievances Under Special Campaign 6, Reclaims 18,644 Sq. Ft. of Office Space
The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), along with its attached and subordinate offices, concluded Special Campaign 6 under the guidance of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). The campaign, aimed at institutionalising the principles of Swachhata (cleanliness) and minimising pendency in official work, was undertaken across all offices to promote cleanliness, efficiency and effective record management.
Special Campaign 6 was conducted from 2nd of October to 31st of October 2026, preceded by a preparatory phase from 15th of September to 30th September 2026. Throughout the campaign, DPIIT undertook focused efforts to promote awareness about cleanliness, systematic record management and the timely disposal of pending cases. With near-total achievement of the identified targets and notable progress across various campaign parameters, DPIIT reaffirmed its commitment to institutionalising Swachhata, fostering a culture of efficiency and responsiveness, and strengthening sustainable practices in government functioning.
As part of the campaign, the National Council for Cement and Building Materials (NCCBM), an autonomous organisation under DPIIT, installed a biomass gasifier at its Ballabgarh campus in Haryana. The gasifier uses biomass, wood and refuse-derived fuel (RDF) as feedstock to produce a combustible gas known as Syngas. During the campaign, NCCBM successfully conducted a trial run using 150 kg of dry horticultural waste. The waste was first shredded and subsequently converted into Syngas through partial oxidation at elevated temperatures under a controlled supply of gasifying agents. The potential utilisation of the Syngas generated through this process in power generation and diesel generator (DG) sets will be explored further. Trial runs using Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) obtained from Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) were also conducted in the gasifier during the campaign. This initiative showcases an environmentally sustainable approach to waste-to-energy conversion and offers a replicable model for promoting sustainable infrastructure, resource recovery and the principles of a circular economy.
In addition to this initiative, DPIIT made significant progress across other key parameters of the campaign. Its attached and subordinate offices undertook the disposal of scrap materials and e-waste, resulting in the reclamation of 18,644 square feet of office space and the generation of ₹16,52,569 in revenue. The Department also achieved 100% completion in the disposal of public grievances and nearly 100% completion across other key parameters, including public grievance appeals, review of e-files and physical files, and cleanliness activities. Central Government Approves ₹10,600 Crore Production Linked Incentive Scheme to Strengthen Technical Textiles Sector: Union Minister of Textiles Shri Giriraj Singh
articles.full_content:
Union Minister of Textiles, Shri Giriraj Singh, today conducted an official inspection of the SRF Limited manufacturing facility situated at the SIPCOT Industrial Park in Gummidipoondi, Tiruvallur district. The facility is engaged in the manufacture of Nylon-6 and Nylon-66, which constitute vital inputs for key industries, including automobile tyres and the defence sector. Tiruvallur District Collector Ms. Kavitha IAS, Member of the Legislative Assembly (Gummidipoondi) Shri Vijayakumar, and senior government officials accompanied the Union Minister during the inspection.
Visiting the various production units of the establishment, the Union Minister reviewed the manufacturing processes and enquired about the range of technical textile products being produced at the plant.
Addressing media representatives following the inspection, Shri Giriraj Singh underscored the pivotal role played by SRF Limited in the domestic production of Nylon-6 and Nylon-66 for strategic sectors such as tyres and defence.
“The Government of India remains steadfastly committed to advancing the growth of the technical textiles sector. Under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government has approved a ₹ 10,600 crore Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme to provide a major impetus to technical textiles,” the Union Minister stated.
Reaffirming the Centre’s continued support for the industry, Shri Giriraj Singh assured that the Government will continue to extend all necessary assistance to leading manufacturing establishments to propel India’s technical textiles sector to the next stage of growth.

The facility is engaged in the manufacture of Nylon-6 and Nylon-66, which constitute vital inputs for key industries, including automobile tyres and the defence sector. Kavitha IAS, Member of the Legislative Assembly (Gummidipoondi) Shri Vijayakumar, and senior government officials accompanied the Union Minister during the inspection.

articles.title: Union Minister of Textiles Shri Giriraj Singh Reviews Textile Sector Initiatives in Tamil Nadu; Emphasises Weaver Welfare, Product Diversification and Export Promotion
articles.full_content:
The Union Minister of Textiles, Shri Giriraj Singh, undertook a series of official engagements in Tamil Nadu on 23 and 24 November 2026, focusing on strengthening the textile and sericulture sectors, promoting industrial development, enhancing weavers’ livelihoods and boosting textile exports.
On 24 November 2026, the Minister chaired a review meeting in Chennai with senior officials from the Central and State Governments associated with the handloom sector, Central Silk Board, PM MITRA Park and various verticals of the textile industry. Representatives from industry and allied sectors also participated in the meeting.
The meeting was attended by Smt. R. Lilly, IAS, Secretary, Handlooms, Handicrafts, Textiles and Khadi Department, Government of Tamil Nadu; Thiru R. Sadheesh, IAS, Director of Sericulture (Full Additional Charge), Government of Tamil Nadu; Thiru S. A. Raman, IAS, Managing Director, SIPCOT; Tmt. P. Uma Maheswari, IAS, Director of Handlooms, Tamil Nadu; Smt. Swayamprava Pani, Additional Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Ministry of Textiles; Shri Anil Kumar, IRS, Director (Infrastructure), Ministry of Textiles; and Shri P. Sivakumar, IFS, Member Secretary, Central Silk Board, along with other senior officials from the Ministry and associated organisations.
The discussions focused on reviewing the progress of the "PM MITRA Park at Virudhunagar, Tamil Nadu"; diversification of silk products in Kanchipuram; enhancement of weavers’ income and revenue; promotion of new-age fibres; and the potential for replicating the successful Kanchipuram cluster model in other textile sectors. The Minister also emphasised the need for a focused and coordinated approach towards promoting textile exports and strengthening India's competitiveness in international markets.
Reiterating the Government's commitment to the welfare of the textile sector, Shri Giriraj Singh emphasised the importance of providing better opportunities, improved facilities and necessary support to weavers, artisans and all stakeholders associated with the textile industry across Tamil Nadu, including Chennai.
Earlier, on 23 November 2026, following the inauguration of the 27th International Congress on Sericulture and Silk Industry (ISCC-2026) and the Silk Mark Expo 2026 in Chennai, The Minister visited the "Perarignar Anna Handloom Silk Park, Kanchipuram". He inspected the handloom units and viewed the silk products of Prakash Silks & Sarees. He also interacted with weavers and the Board of Directors to review the progress of the project and understand the facilities and opportunities available to the weaving community. Emphasising the importance of strengthening traditional silk weaving, he highlighted the need for improved infrastructure, better facilities and enhanced market opportunities to increase weavers’ income and take Kanchipuram’s rich silk heritage to greater heights.
